name: Kilimanjaro Machame Route
summary: The busiest of the southern approaches, climbing from Machame Gate past the Shira plateau and the Lava Tower, then along the southern circuit to Barafu for the summit night on Uhuru Peak. Descent is by the Mweka trail, so the walk crosses the mountain rather than returning the way it came.

name: Kilimanjaro Lemosho Route
summary: A western approach that begins in forest at Londorossi and crosses the Shira plateau before joining the southern circuit to Barafu and Uhuru Peak. The extra days low down give more time to acclimatise than the shorter southern routes.

name: Kilimanjaro Rongai Route
summary: The only route that climbs Kilimanjaro from the north, starting near the Kenyan border on the drier side of the mountain and reaching the crater rim at Gilman's Point before Uhuru Peak. Descent is by the Marangu trail on the south side.

name: Kilimanjaro Northern Circuit
summary: The longest route on the mountain, starting from the west and swinging right around the quiet northern slopes before turning up to Uhuru Peak from School Hut. The added days are spent walking at altitude, which is why operators report the highest summit rates on it.

name: Kilimanjaro Marangu Route
summary: The oldest route, and the only one with sleeping huts rather than tents, climbing the south-east side to Gilman's Point on the crater rim and along it to Uhuru Peak. Ascent and descent use the same trail, and the short five-day version leaves little room to acclimatise.

name: Mount Meru Trek
summary: The Momella route through Arusha National Park to Socialist Peak, walked with an armed ranger because the lower forest holds buffalo and elephant. The summit day follows a narrow crater rim in the dark and is often used as acclimatisation before Kilimanjaro.

name: Mount Kenya Sirimon Route
summary: The north-western approach up the Mackinder Valley to Shipton's Camp and on to Point Lenana, the trekking summit below the rock peaks of Batian and Nelion. Gradients are gentler than the other main routes, and it is often paired with a Chogoria descent.

name: Mount Kenya Chogoria Route
summary: The eastern approach, past the Nithi Falls, Lake Michaelson and the Gorges Valley to Point Lenana. It gains height more slowly than the western routes and is commonly walked as a descent after ascending by Sirimon.

name: Mount Kenya Naro Moru Route
summary: The shortest and steepest way to Point Lenana, up the Teleki Valley through the section known as the vertical bog to Mackinder's Camp. The speed of the ascent gives the least time to acclimatise of the three main routes.

name: Rwenzori Central Circuit
summary: The original loop from Nyakalengija up the Mubuku and Bujuku valleys, over the Scott Elliot Pass to the Kitandara lakes and back through the Freshfield area. Much of it is deep bog and root ladders under near-permanent cloud; the glaciated climb of Margherita Peak on Mount Stanley is a technical add-on, not part of the trek.

name: Rwenzori Kilembe Trail
summary: The southern approach from Kilembe up the Nyamwamba valley through Mutinda and Bugata to the Bamwanjara Pass and the Kitandara lakes. Conditions are as wet and boggy as the Central Circuit; itineraries that continue to Margherita Peak add a glacier climb requiring rope, crampons and axe.

name: Simien Mountains Trek
summary: A walk along the escarpment from Debark through Sankaber, Geech and Chennek, with gelada troops and Walia ibex on the cliff edge. Shorter itineraries turn back at the Bwahit Pass around 4,200 m; the longer ones cross into the Meshaha valley and climb Ras Dashen at 4,550 m, which is the figure given here.

name: Bale Mountains Trek
summary: A horse-supported walk out of Dinsho across the Sanetti plateau, the largest area of Afro-alpine terrain in Africa and the best place to see the Ethiopian wolf. Gradients are mostly gentle but the route stays above 3,500 m for days and crosses Tullu Dimtu at 4,377 m; the park also sells much shorter and much longer variants.
